title.en: GSEQ complete elliptic integrals K(m), E(m) approximation

summary: Evaluate the GSEQ apx==1 polynomial-logarithmic approximation of the complete elliptic integrals K(m) and E(m) on the squared-modulus convention, with the source's whole-array singular guard preserved verbatim.

identity.relation: K(m), E(m) from nested polynomial-logarithmic evaluation: K = a_k(p) - b_k(p)*log(p), E = a_e(p) - b_e(p)*log(p) with p = 1 - m and the source's hardcoded polynomial coefficients.
identity.direction: squared modulus m in [0, 1] -> complete elliptic integrals K(m) and E(m)
identity.definition: The source's apx==1 approximation for the GSEQ coil Green function. The singular guard is a WHOLE-ARRAY test `if (k2 == 1.0)`: when every element equals 1 the source returns the finite sentinel K = 1.0e300, E = 1; when any element differs the polynomial-log branch runs and m == 1 elements yield K = +Inf and E = NaN (0 * -Inf). Both paths are reproduced verbatim; the encoded singular returns are contract, not input errors.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation, ported verbatim including the vector guard
identity.boundary: finite inputs in [0, 1] only; the m == 1 sentinel/Inf/NaN returns are encoded source singular boundaries
assumptions: The approximation is the source's own special-function implementation, kept for GSEQ provenance parity; it is not the most accurate K/E evaluation available.
No external physics reference is bound: accuracy is quantified against scipy's ellipk/ellipe as sampled evidence.

outputs.name: complete_k
outputs.description: First-kind complete elliptic integral K(m), source approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite for m < 1; whole-array m == 1 yields the finite sentinel 1.0e300; mixed arrays yield +Inf at m == 1 elements.

outputs.name: complete_e
outputs.description: Second-kind complete elliptic integral E(m), source approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite for m < 1; whole-array m == 1 yields 1; mixed arrays yield NaN at m == 1 elements.

preconditions: Squared moduli from a caller (e.g. the coil Green geometry operator) in [0, 1].
supported: Source apx==1 K(m), E(m) evaluation for GSEQ Green-response provenance parity.
excluded: High-precision K/E evaluation (use a scientific library), modulus generation, coil geometry, and the Green field responses.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any entry is non-finite or outside [0, 1].
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Not applicable; the m == 1 sentinel/Inf/NaN returns are encoded source singular boundaries, not runtime failures.

The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison; qualified-L1 delivery root remains empty, so this is not qualified-L1 provenance and not expert approval.

example.description: Evaluate the approximation on a few moduli; values are finite for m < 1 and the whole-array m == 1 sentinel is reproduced.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals
k, e = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 0.9]))
assert np.all(np.isfinite(k)) and np.all(np.isfinite(e))
k1, e1 = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([1.0]))
assert k1[0] == 1.0e300 and e1[0] == 1.0
km, em = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 1.0]))
assert np.isinf(km[1]) and np.isnan(em[1])
example.expected: Finite K/E for m < 1; the whole-array m == 1 sentinel (K=1e300, E=1) and the mixed-array Inf/NaN singular path are both reproduced.

scope: Source polynomial-log evaluation against an independent recomputation.
Encoded singular boundaries and input failure contracts.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests establish the polynomial-log evaluation against an independent recomputation (exact array equality), the whole-array sentinel and mixed-array Inf/NaN singular paths, and the fail-closed domain contract. Sampled accuracy evidence: on a 200,001-point sweep of m in [1e-6, 0.999999] the approximation agrees with scipy.special.ellipk/ellipe to at most 1e-8 relative in K and 2e-8 relative in E; this is sampled evidence, not a bound over the continuous domain, and the baseline filament assets are not required to reproduce it.
known_limitations: The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.
The approximation is less accurate than library special functions (~1e-8 relative sampled); consumers needing higher accuracy should use the baseline scipy-elliptic filament relation instead.
The mixed-array m == 1 path returns Inf/NaN by source contract; the companion Green-response operator rejects the corresponding geometry rather than consuming it.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
